title: Mi · ci · mu · jej · nam · wam · im
note:
B1 Block 5, unit 2. A2's dat_chunks fenced the pronoun set to mi/mnie only, in three fixed blocks (podoba mi się, smakuje mi, boli mnie). This unit completes the pronoun grid — ci, mu, jej, nam, wam, im — and generalises it onto the two verbs that are genuinely dative-governing in every person: podobać się (full paradigm, the real payoff) and smakować (partial spread: mu, im only, load control). boleć is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED — it takes the accusative in every person (boli mnie/cię/go/ją...), a different pronoun set the course has not taught, and generalising the new dative pronouns onto it would be a genuine grammar error, not a simplification; a2_dat_chunks's own note already flagged that boli mnie is accusative, not dative, and left it unexplained on purpose. This unit does not touch that fence.

HOMOGRAPH, flagged loudly and predicted in advance by b1_virile_reco's own digest note: ci already exists in the taught pool as the virile demonstrative (ci studenci = 'these students', b1_virile_reco). This unit re-teaches the identical string as a completely unrelated word: the 2sg dative clitic (podoba ci się = 'you like it'). The auditor cannot see this — it only matches strings, and ci is already 'taught' by an earlier pack. Disambiguated explicitly: intro slide 2 puts both meanings side by side by name, and quiz item 9 places a real sentence using virile ci (Ci nauczyciele pomagają studentowi) next to items using dative ci, so both senses are seen in genuine context rather than through a meta 'which meaning' question (Kontrola stage forbids meta-questions about the language).

Only 6 teaches_lemmas (ci, mu, jej, nam, wam, im) — deliberately light, same precedent as b1_virile_past: the payload here is completing a paradigm and disambiguating a homograph, not new vocabulary. Both-gender-neutral (the dative pronouns do not mark gender except jej/mu, which are already gender-specific by definition).

intro.title: The pronoun set, completed
intro.body: You have owned mi since A1 (chce mi się) and used it constantly since a2_dat_chunks (podoba mi się). It was never the whole set — just the I-form. Here is the rest of it, for the same to/for job.
intro.body_pl: mi (ja, już twoje) + ci, mu, jej, nam, wam, im — nowe.

intro.title: Warning: you already know a word spelled ci
intro.body:
You met ci recently meaning these — ci studenci, ci nauczyciele, a group with at least one man. That ci is completely unrelated to this one. They are two different words that happen to be spelled the same, like English course (school subject) and course (a meal).

The test: demonstrative ci always stands right before a plural person-noun (ci studenci). Dative ci always stands next to a verb, with no noun following it directly (podoba ci się).
intro.body_pl: Ci studenci pracują. (ci = studenci) ≠ Podoba ci się. (ci = ty, celownik)

rows: stands next to a verb, no noun after

intro.title: podobać się, complete
intro.body: Every person of like it, in one table. The pattern from a2_dat_chunks never changes — verb, pronoun, się — only the pronoun moves.
intro.body_pl: Podoba mi się. Podoba ci się? Podoba mu się. Podoba jej się. Podoba nam się. Podoba wam się? Podoba im się.

intro.title: Same pronouns, smakować — but not boleć
intro.body:
smakować works the same way — good taste happens to someone. Smakuje mu. Smakuje im.

boleć does NOT take these pronouns, even though it looked like part of the same family in a2_dat_chunks. Boli mnie uses a completely different pronoun set (mnie there is accusative, not dative) that this course has not taught yet. Keep boleć exactly as you learned it — boli mnie/cię is not built from today's table.
intro.body_pl: Smakuje mu ta zupa. Smakuje im to wino. (boleć: bez zmian, poza zakresem)

oni or one → im, the same word either way.

quiz.explain: Same to/for pronoun set works on smakować too — on → mu.
This is the OTHER ci — the demonstrative one, right before the plural noun nauczyciele. Not the pronoun from today's table.
nie in front of the whole block, exactly like nie podoba mi się — only the pronoun changed.

type_items.explain: This is the dative ci — a different word from the ci in ci studenci, just spelled the same.
Same word for oni and one — the dative pronoun does not carry the virile split.
